Chembra Peak

17 km

The highest peak in Wayanad, Chembra is a trekker’s paradise offering panoramic views of misty hills and valleys. Its highlight is the heart-shaped lake, believed to never dry up, which makes the trek both romantic and adventurous. Surrounded by lush greenery and tea plantations, Chembra Peak is a must-visit for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

Pookode Lake

13 Km

A natural freshwater lake surrounded by evergreen forests and rolling hills, Pookode is one of Wayanad’s most popular attractions. Its tranquil waters are perfect for boating, while the surrounding area offers walking trails, a children’s park, and opportunities to spot local wildlife. With its serene ambience and scenic beauty, Pookode Lake is an ideal stop for families and nature lovers.

Lakkidi View Point

16 Km

Known as the “Gateway of Wayanad,” Lakkidi View Point offers breathtaking panoramic views of mist-covered valleys, winding ghat roads, and lush forests. Perched at a high altitude, it is one of the most scenic spots in the region, especially at sunrise and sunset. With its cool climate and enchanting landscapes, Lakkidi is a must-visit for travelers seeking unforgettable photo opportunities and serene natural beauty.

 

Soochipara Falls

22 km

     4.2 Out of 8 Google Reviews

Also known as Sentinel Rock Waterfalls, Soochipara is a stunning three-tiered cascade set amidst dense forests near Meppadi. The trek to the falls takes you through scenic trails, and the plunge pool at the base is perfect for swimming and relaxation. Surrounded by towering cliffs ideal for rock climbing, Soochipara is a must-visit for adventure seekers and nature lovers.

900 Kandi

20–25 km

An offbeat gem hidden in the forests of Wayanad, 900 Kandi is a paradise for adventure seekers. Famous for its glass bridge offering breathtaking views of the dense greenery below, it also features trekking trails, camping spots, and thrilling jeep rides through rugged terrain. With its untouched natural beauty and adrenaline-filled experiences, 900 Kandi is perfect for those looking to explore Wayanad’s wild side.

Karappuzha Dam

8 KM

Karapuzha Tourist Park in Wayanad is a scenic adventure destination located near the Karapuzha Dam, offering Kerala’s longest zipline, boating, gardens, and family-friendly attractions amidst the lush Western Ghats. It’s a perfect blend of nature and thrill, making it one of Wayanad’s most popular tourist spots.

Myladippara

0 KM

Myladippara is a serene viewpoint near Kalpetta in Wayanad, Kerala, known for its panoramic views of lush valleys and hills. It’s a peaceful spot ideal for trekking, birdwatching, photography, and picnics, with no entry fee and open daily from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

Kurumbalakotta View Point

15 KM

Kurumbalakotta View Point in Wayanad is a stunning monolithic hill offering 360° panoramic views of the Western Ghats, including Chembra Peak, Banasura Mala, and Ambukuthi Mala. It is especially famous for its breathtaking sunrise and sunset views, making it a must-visit spot for trekkers and nature lovers.

Cholamala Waterfalls

12 Km

Cholamala Waterfalls in Wayanad is a hidden natural gem, tucked away in the lush forests near Meppadi. It’s a relatively less-crowded spot, offering a peaceful escape with cascading waters surrounded by greenery and rocky terrain.

content.rendered:
Edakkal Caves

25 Km

The Edakkal Caves are one of Wayanad’s most fascinating historical attractions, known for their ancient rock carvings that date back thousands of years. Located high on Ambukuthi Hills, the caves offer a short trekking experience along with breathtaking views of the surrounding landscapes. A visit here combines adventure, history, and nature, making it a must-see destination for travelers exploring Kerala

Wayanad / Muthanga Wildlife Sanctuary

15 Km

Nestled along the Kerala–Karnataka border, Muthanga Wildlife Sanctuary is part of the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary, which in turn forms a vital section of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Spread across lush forests and grasslands, it is home to a rich variety of flora and fauna, making it a paradise for nature lovers and wildlife enthusiasts.

Visitors can spot elephants, tigers, leopards, deer, bison, and exotic bird species during safaris, while the sanctuary’s dense forests of teak, bamboo, and eucalyptus add to its scenic charm. It is also a haven for birdwatchers, with hornbills, peacocks, and woodpeckers among the highlights.

📍 Location: 15 km from Sulthan Bathery, Wayanad, Kerala

🕒 Safari Timings: Morning and evening slots (subject to forest department schedule) 🎟

Entry: Nominal fee; guided jeep safaris available

Jain Temple

0 KM

The Jain Temple at Sulthan Bathery is one of the most remarkable heritage sites in Wayanad. Built in the 13th century in the Vijayanagara architectural style, it reflects the region’s once‑flourishing Jain culture. The temple features ornate stone pillars, carved motifs of swans and snakes, and a raised stone platform, showcasing exquisite craftsmanship.

In the 18th century, Tipu Sultan used the temple as an ammunition store, adding a layer of historical intrigue to its legacy. Today, it stands as a protected monument, more of a cultural landmark than an active place of worship, drawing visitors interested in history, architecture, and spirituality.

📍 Location: Sulthan Bathery, Wayanad, Kerala

🕒 Timings: 8:00 AM – 12:00 PM, 2:00 PM – 6:00 PM 🎟

Entry: Free

Wayanad Heritage Museum

12 KM

The Wayanad Heritage Museum, located at Ambalavayal near Sulthan Bathery, is one of Kerala’s largest and most important archaeological museums. It offers a fascinating glimpse into the region’s rich history, culture, and tribal traditions.

The museum houses an impressive collection of tribal artifacts, ancient weapons, stone carvings, terracotta figures, hunting tools, musical instruments, and household items dating back to the Neolithic age. Visitors can explore exhibits that highlight the lifestyle and artistry of Wayanad’s indigenous communities, making it a cultural treasure trove.

Location: Ambalavayal, 12 km from Sulthan Bathery, Wayanad, Kerala

Timings: 9:00 AM – 5:30 PM (closed on Mondays)

  Entry: Nominal fee

Manjappare View point

12 km

Manjappara View Point near Sulthan Bathery is a hidden gem in Wayanad, offering breathtaking 360° views of valleys, forests, and the Western Ghats. Known for its spectacular sunrise and sunset vistas, it’s a free, easily accessible spot perfect for photography and nature lovers.

Location: Ambalavayal, 12 km from Sulthan Bathery, Wayanad, Kerala

Timings: 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM (best time to visit -Early morning or sunset)

  Entry: Free

Nellarachal View Point

17.5 KM

Nellarachal View Point is a scenic hilltop destination in Wayanad, offering stunning views of the Karapuzha Dam backwaters, rolling hills, and lush green valleys. It’s a peaceful spot away from the crowds, perfect for travelers seeking tranquility and natural beauty.

From the viewpoint, visitors can enjoy panoramic landscapes, misty mornings, and colorful sunsets, making it a favorite for photographers and nature lovers. The calm surroundings and fresh air create an ideal setting for relaxation or a short break during your Wayanad explorations.

📍 Location: Near Sulthan Bathery, Wayanad, Kerala

🕒 Timings: Open daily, best visited early morning or evening

🎟 Entry: Free

Tholpetty Wildlife Sanctuary

20 KM

Tholpetty Wildlife Sanctuary, located in the northern part of Wayanad near Sulthan Bathery, is a vibrant stretch of forest that forms part of the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary and the larger Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Known for its rich biodiversity, the sanctuary is a haven for wildlife enthusiasts and adventure seekers.

Visitors can enjoy thrilling jeep safaris through dense forests, where sightings of elephants, tigers, leopards, bison, deer, and a wide variety of birds are common. The sanctuary’s mix of moist deciduous forests and bamboo groves creates a picturesque setting, perfect for photography and nature walks.

📍 Location: About 20 km from Mananthavady, easily accessible from Sulthan Bathery

🕒 Safari Timings: Morning and evening slots (organized by the forest department)

🎟 Entry: Nominal fee; guided jeep safaris available

Kuruva Island

17 KM

Kuruva Island (also called Kuruvadweep) is a cluster of lush, uninhabited islets spread across the serene Kabini River. Known for its untouched natural beauty, the island is covered with dense evergreen forests, bamboo groves, and rare medicinal plants, making it a paradise for eco‑tourists and nature lovers.

Visitors can enjoy bamboo rafting, nature walks, birdwatching, and spotting butterflies, while the calm river waters and greenery create a tranquil escape. The island is also home to migratory birds and unique flora, offering a refreshing break from city life.

📍 Location: About 17 km from Mananthavady, Wayanad, Kerala

🕒 Timings: 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM (entry regulated by forest department)

🎟 Entry: Nominal fee; guided eco‑tourism activities available

Pakshipathalam Bird Sanctuary

36 KM

Pakshipathalam Bird Sanctuary in Wayanad is a paradise for birdwatchers and trekkers, located in the Brahmagiri Hills at about 1,740 m above sea level. Accessible only by a forest trek starting near Thirunelli Temple, it offers rare bird sightings, caves, and panoramic views, making it one of Kerala’s most adventurous eco‑tourism spots.

📍 Location: About  km from Mananthavady, Wayanad, Kerala

🕒 Timings: :6:00 AM – 6:00 PM 

🎟 Entry: ₹50 (Indians), ₹200 (Foreign nationals).

Thirunelli Temple

30 KM

Nestled in the Brahmagiri Hills at an altitude of about 900 m, Thirunelli Temple is one of Kerala’s most ancient and revered shrines. Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, the temple is often called the “Kashi of the South” because of its spiritual significance and its association with ancestral rites.

Surrounded by forests and streams, the temple is believed to have been built over a thousand years ago. Its stone‑pillared architecture, serene setting, and the nearby Papanasini stream (where devotees perform rituals for departed souls) make it a unique blend of natural beauty and sacred tradition.

📍 Location: Thirunelli, about 30 km from Mananthavady and accessible from Sulthan Bathery

🕒 Timings: 5:30 AM – 12:00 PM, 5:30 PM – 8:00 PM 🎟

Entry: Free

Banasura Sagar Dam

21 KM

4.8 Out of 8 Google Reviews

Banasura Sagar Dam, located about 21 km from Kalpetta in Wayanad, is the largest earthen dam in India and the second largest of its kind in Asia. Built across the Karamanathodu tributary of the Kabini River, the dam is surrounded by mist‑clad hills and lush greenery, making it one of the most scenic attractions in the region.

The dam creates a vast reservoir dotted with small islands, offering breathtaking views and opportunities for boating, trekking, and picnics. Adventure seekers can explore nearby trails leading up to the Banasura Hills, while families enjoy the serene waters and landscaped gardens around the dam.

📍 Location: Padinjarathara, about 21 km from Mananthavady, Wayanad, Kerala

Near Aiswarya Cineplex

4.7 Out of 1019 Google Reviews

Near Jubilee resturant

     3.9  Out of 211 Google Reviews

Mathais Resto Cafe

Dhottapankulam

4.8 Out of 14842 Google Reviews

Wilton Hotel & Restaurant

Dhottappankulam

4.6 Out of 26k Google Reviews

Wilton Family Restaurant in Sulthan Bathery is one of the most iconic dining spots in Wayanad, rated 4.8/5 . It’s the largest restaurant in the district, seating over 300 guests, and is famous for its beef ribs biryani, seafood, and multi-cuisine offerings.

Jubilee Restaurant

Sulthan Bathery

4.3 Out of 14.75k Google Reviews

Jubilee Family Restaurant in Sulthan Bathery is one of the oldest and most respected dining spots in Wayanad, founded in 1996. It’s famous for its Malabar biryanis, Kerala curries, and North Indian dishes, offering a “royal” breakfast, lunch, and dinner experience. Rated around 4.2–4.3/5, it combines tradition with modern service, making it a landmark restaurant in the region

Ruchippura

Opposite to Wilton hotel

4.1 Out of 209 Google Reviews

Ruchippura Restaurant in Sulthan Bathery is a well-loved local spot offering authentic Kerala village-style flavors, especially seafood and traditional meals. Rated around 4.1/5, it’s praised for its fried fish, biryani, and homely breakfast items like idli, dosa, and chutneys, all at very budget-friendly prices

 

Mysore Veg Cafe

Near Aiswarya Cineplux

     4.7 Out of 1839 Google Reviews

Mysore Veg Cafe in Sulthan Bathery is a top-rated pure vegetarian restaurant (Google rating 4.7/5) offering South Indian, North Indian, Chinese, and Udupi-style dishes. It’s especially famous for its masala dosa, idli, vada, and strong filter coffee, making it one of the most recommended veg dining spots in Wayanad

Dil Pot

Dhottappankulam

4.5 Out of 268 Google Reviews

Dilpot Restaurant in Sulthan Bathery is a multi-cuisine eatery offering North Indian, Chinese, Kerala-style dishes, and Arabian specialties like mandi and alfaham. It’s located in Royal Gallery, Dhottappankulam, and is known for its wide menu variety, though reviews suggest mixed ratings (around 3.2/5)
